source.title: It Takes 8 Tokens: Weak-to-Strong Off-Policy RL via Auxiliary Branches
source.authors: Dayu Wang; Jia-Ye Yang; Wei-Kang Li; Jia-Hui Liang; Li-Wei Qian; Xin Pei; Ji-Zhou Huang

page_placements.theme: Weaker models' reasoning traces, drafts, critiques or exploration branches, filtered or rewarded with ground truth, improve a stronger model's training

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites weak-to-strong learning and uses a weaker model as a source of short reasoning branches, but evaluates its own verifier-based RL method. It does not test fine-tuning on weak-model labels or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern W2SPO, which inserts short auxiliary-model branches into target-model trajectories and trains from final verifier rewards. The auxiliary model does not label training examples, and the paper does not compare a weak supervisor's task score with a strong student's score or calculate PGR. The W2SPO results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of V1–V6.
record.test_reason: W2SPO trains a 4B target with ground-truth verifier rewards. A frozen weaker model (Gemma-3-4B-IT, 40.7% overall vs the target's 58.3%) only proposes 8-token branches and never labels training data. There is no weak-label fine-tuning, no weak supervisor ceiling comparison and no PGR. The paper borrows the weak-to-strong framing (it cites Burns et al. 2023) and reports only its own method against GRPO, ablations and other 4B models. This is T4: no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that weak auxiliary branches give useful local exploration signals. They report that W2SPO beats matched-sampling GRPO and target-only branching while better preserving Pass@k, and they limit scope to small models and math tasks.
record.recipe_differences: W2SPO is off-policy verifier-based RL: a frozen auxiliary model proposes short segments, the target model completes each trajectory, and policy updates apply only to the inserted branch tokens. It does not fine-tune a strong model on labels produced by a weak supervisor.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported results vary by benchmark and, in robustness experiments, by random seed and auxiliary-model choice. Branch insertion position and length also vary in the inference intervention experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Short (8-token) branches from a frozen weaker model, inserted into target trajectories and scored by ground-truth verifiers, raise greedy Pass@1. Overall rises from 62.3% (matched GRPO) and 61.9% (A-only branches) to 64.2%. They also increase distinct correct trajectories at inference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In verifier-based reasoning RL, a weaker frozen model can serve as a local exploration proposer that improves a stronger target's performance, without supplying labels.

record.problems: The study does not measure PGR or compare the target against the auxiliary model as a weak labeler. Main benchmark scores are point estimates without reported error bars; robustness checks include a different seed and auxiliary model. The authors limit the scope to relatively small-scale language models and mathematical reasoning tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were left out. Runtime comparisons and training-time diagnostics were omitted because they measure efficiency or reward-signal properties rather than the related auxiliary-branch task outcome.

untested.parts: No strong student fine-tuned on weak-model labels; no PGR or strong ceiling. Training reward is ground-truth verifier correctness.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembles or loss variants compared on PGR. The ablations concern the authors' RL branch method.
No variation of supervisor or student size, task family or representations with PGR.
No weak-label exploitation, distribution-shift PGR or correlated-error analysis.
Appendix B analysis concerns branch-level policy gradients and all-wrong group probability. It is not about conditions under which a student beats its supervisor.
Language and math only; no vision.

record.verdict_notes: 'Weak-to-strong' is used here loosely: the weak model proposes exploration tokens and supervision comes from ground-truth answers. The 'Different B Model' (Mistral-7B) is not smaller than the 4B target. Main accuracy numbers are single-run point estimates with one extra seed; AIME scores move by 6.7 points across seeds.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on weak-supervisor labels, weak-supervisor performance comparison, or PGR.
Does not test whether the named training changes raise PGR over naive fine-tuning.
No PGR comparison by supervisor or student size, task family, or representation.
Does not test the specified weak-label failure modes or measure PGR under distribution shift or correlated errors.
No theory about conditions for a student trained on weak labels to beat its supervisor.
Experiments are on language models and mathematical reasoning, not vision.

relation.reason: The weaker frozen model supplies local branches; ground-truth rule-based rewards supply supervision. No catalog claim version is tested.

tranche.reason: Uses weak auxiliary proposals as an exploration tool and reports its own verifier-based RL performance; it does not test weak-label generalization or PGR.

source_check.notes: All 25 listed numerical comparisons are accurate. Their local performance states should not serve as claim states: R1–R7 are inference interventions and R8–R25 are the study's own method comparisons; retain only as contextual results with versions=none. The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate.
